lines.trans: What a glorious Saturday morning for a treasure walk down Jasmine Street!
Let us check the brass compass first: east runs straight toward the corner bakery.
Read Clue Card One aloud, Nour, so we do not miss a single word.
Card One says: Twenty paces east where cool clear water greets the morning birds.
Easy! That is the little carved stone fountain at the end of our block!
Wait, Rami—whose paces are we counting, yours or mine?
Good question, because Rami walks like he is chasing a departing bus!
Very funny, Nour; let us walk side by side at a polite normal step.
Five, ten, fifteen... eighteen, nineteen, and twenty paces right to the kerb!
Look ahead—two sparrows are splashing on the rim of the stone fountain!
Thirty years later, the morning birds are still keeping their appointment!
Now look closely at Card One to see what symbol we need to find.

meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite noun without ال- to mean 'the last' (آخر يوم 'the last day', آخر الساحة 'the far end of the courtyard').

examples.trans: The attic room is at the end of the floor.
Today is the last day of the week.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of اتجه. With بـ, باتجاه means 'toward' (باتجاه الشباك 'toward the window').

examples.trans: He raised his cup toward the room's window.
He pointed us in the direction of the bus station.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستقبل, بيستقبل).

examples.trans: Let us go down to welcome the new guest.
They welcomed us with a smile and hot tea.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait just a minute.

examples.text: استنى شوي، أنا نازل معك هسه!
examples.trans: Wait a second—I'm coming down with you right now!

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: The man who I saw yesterday.

examples.text: هذا المحل اللي اشترينا منه الكنافة الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: This is the shop where we bought the kunafa last week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: باردة, plural: باردين).

examples.trans: Here, drink a glass of cold water.
My hands were cold from the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: باصات.

examples.trans: The bus station is close to here.
The bus trip was comfortable.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بسيطة, plural: بسيطين).

examples.trans: Explain the matter to me in simple words.
The problem is minor and easy to fix.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: After a plural verb, بعض means 'each other' (بننادي بعض 'we call each other').

examples.trans: We call each other by first name here.

examples.text: ما حكينا مع بعض من زمان.
examples.trans: We have not spoken with each other in a long time.

meanings.note: Used for navigation or metaphorically for direction.

examples.text: ضاع بالصحراء لأنه ما كان معه بوصلة.
examples.trans: He got lost in the desert because he didn't have a compass.

examples.text: اتبعنا إبرة البوصلة لحد ما وصلنا الشرق.
examples.trans: We followed the compass needle until we reached the east.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian and Levantine word used as a possessive marker, similar to "of" or "'s".

examples.trans: My brother's car is broken.
Where is the key belonging to the kitchen cupboard?

meanings.note: Colloquial Jordanian numeral for 19 (also تسعطعشر before singular nouns).

examples.text: عدينا تسعطعش خطوة لحد زاوية الحيط.
examples.trans: We counted nineteen steps up to the corner of the wall.
He is nineteen years old and works at the bakery.

meanings.note: The number 30.

examples.trans: His age is now thirty years.

examples.text: ضلينا تلاتين دقيقة بنستنى الكيكة تبرد.
examples.trans: We spent thirty minutes waiting for the cake to cool.

meanings.note: Colloquial Jordanian numeral for 18 (also تمنطعش).

examples.trans: We walked eighteen paces and then stopped.

examples.text: عنده ثمنطعش كتاب عن النباتات والأعشاب.
examples.trans: He has eighteen books on plants and herbs.

meanings.note: Commonly used preposition for indicating proximity, next to, or beside.

examples.trans: Sit next to your brother.
We set the trays next to the fountain in the shade.

meanings.note: Standard word for a stone or rock, singular form.

examples.trans: We found a strange stone in the garden.

examples.text: لقينا حجر منحوت عليه نجمة صغيرة.
examples.trans: We found a stone with a small star carved on it.

meanings.note: Used to refer to the edge of a table, cliff, or any physical boundary.

examples.text: دير بالك، الكاسة على حفة الطاولة.
examples.trans: Watch out, the cup is on the edge of the table.

examples.text: لا تحطي الفنجان على حفة الطاولة عشان ما يوقع.
examples.trans: Do not set the cup on the edge of the table so it does not fall.

meanings.note: One of the most frequently used adjectives in Jordanian Arabic to mean beautiful, sweet, nice, or good.

examples.trans: This dress is very beautiful on you.

examples.text: طعم العسل مع قشر البرتقال حلو ومتوازن.
examples.trans: The taste of honey with orange peel is sweet and balanced.

meanings.note: A literal physical step or a metaphorical step in a process.

examples.trans: Let's walk step by step.

examples.text: كل خطوة بهاللغز بتقربنا من المخبز القديم.
examples.trans: Every step in this puzzle brings us closer to the old bakery.

meanings.note: Imperative forms with object pronouns give خليكم بحالكم ('stay in your own business') and خلوني بحالي ('leave me in mine').

examples.trans: Let me speak for a bit.
Stay calm, Mariam.

meanings.note: The number five, used in counting abstractly or before masculine counted nouns.

examples.trans: I bought five books today.

examples.text: عندنا خمسة أبواب خشب بتطلع عالحديقة.
examples.trans: We have five wooden doors leading out to the garden.

meanings.note: Colloquial Jordanian numeral for 15 (also خمسطعشر before singular nouns).

examples.trans: It is three-fifteen right now.
We walked fifteen steps up to the tree.

meanings.note: Essential Jordanian word used for giving directions ('go straight') or to mean doing something immediately.

examples.trans: Walk straight and then turn right.

examples.text: امشي دغري لعند القوس وبعدين لف يسار.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead to the arch and then turn left.

meanings.note: Can mean evidence, proof, or a guide (both a person and a guidebook).

examples.trans: Do you have evidence for what you're saying?

examples.text: هادا الرقم الصغير هو أول دليل للوصول للكنز.
examples.trans: This small number is the first clue for reaching the treasure.

meanings.note: Common everyday verb for 'went' in the past tense. Also used as a future particle.

examples.trans: He went to work in the morning.

examples.text: رامي راح عالمكتبة يدور على الكتاب القديم.
examples.trans: Rami went to the library to look for the old book.

meanings.note: Active participle of راح ('to go'), used like a present progressive in Levantine ('am/is/are going').

examples.text: أنا وسلمى رايحين عالسوق نجيب ليمون.
examples.trans: Salma and I are heading to the market to get lemons.

examples.text: وين رايح بهالسلة الكبيرة يا زياد؟
examples.trans: Where are you heading with that big basket, Ziad?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أرصفة.

examples.trans: The car pulled up beside the pavement.
We walked along the wide sidewalk downtown.

meanings.note: Refers to map symbols, emblems, or passwords.

examples.text: شو الرمز اللي لازم نلاقيه عالكرت الأول؟
examples.trans: What is the symbol that we need to find on the first card?
The jasmine tree is a symbol of hospitality in this house.

meanings.note: Refers to a corner of a room or street, or a geometric angle.

examples.trans: Put the chair in the corner.
The chest is placed in the northern corner of the room.

meanings.note: Used almost universally in the Levantine adverbial phrase بالزبط (biz-zabt, 'exactly / right on').

examples.text: هاد هو اللون الأخضر اللي بدنا إياه بالزبط!
examples.trans: That is the exact shade of green we want!

examples.text: وصل السايق عالباب الساعة تنتين بالزبط.
examples.trans: The driver arrived at the gate at two o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Often used as a cognate object with سأل (سألتك سؤال 'she asked you a question').

examples.trans: I have just one question.
The question was very easy.

meanings.note: Primary weekday meaning is Saturday (يوم السبت); as a rural/Levantine noun can also mean a woven basket.

examples.text: سوق العسل بنفتح كل يوم سبت الصبح.
examples.trans: The honey market opens every Saturday morning.

examples.text: السبت الجاي رح نروح نجمع التوت من المزرعة.
examples.trans: Next Saturday we will go pick berries from the farm.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: This car is this year's model.

examples.text: مرّت سنة كاملة على آخر زيارة للمزرعة.
examples.trans: A whole year has passed since the last visit to the farm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Cardinal direction noun; frequently appears in directional phrases like للشرق or باتجاه الشرق.

examples.text: اتجهنا ناحية الشرق مع ضو الشمس الصبح.
examples.trans: We headed toward the east with the morning sunlight.
The big window faces directly east.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian interrogative pronoun for 'what'.

examples.trans: What are you doing here?

examples.text: شو المكون السري اللي ضفتيه عالعجينة؟
examples.trans: What is the secret ingredient that you added to the batter?

meanings.note: Describes a pure musical note, clear sky (سما صافية), or clear broth.

examples.text: نغمة البيانو طلعت صافية متل المي.
examples.trans: The piano note rang out crystal clear.

examples.text: انشالله تضل السما صافية طول نهار التنين.
examples.trans: Hopefully the sky stays clear all day Monday.

meanings.note: Standard word for morning in both Classical and colloquial Arabic.

examples.trans: The weather is nice this morning.

examples.text: نسمات الصباح بالحديقة بتجيب ريحة الياسمين.
examples.trans: The morning breezes in the garden carry the scent of jasmine.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.text: عندي أخ صغير عمره خمس سنين.
examples.trans: I have a young brother who is five years old.

examples.text: في مفتاح نحاس صغير مخبي تحت الورقة.
examples.trans: There is a small brass key hidden under the sheet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أصوات.

examples.trans: I heard the sound of rain on the window.
His voice is calm and polite on the phone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضيع, بيضيع).

examples.text: الورق لسه بيشتغل لما بتنقطع الكهربا.
examples.trans: Paper still works when the power goes out.
Mazen always misplaces his glasses!

meanings.note: Expressive quadriliteral verb describing water, batter, or ink splashing onto surfaces.

examples.text: المي باردة وعم تطرطش على حفة النافورة.
examples.trans: The water is cold and splashing onto the edge of the fountain.
The ink splattered onto the sheet by mistake.

meanings.note: Both a singular noun (a bird) and a generic collective in Jordanian Arabic; plural طيور.

examples.text: في طير أزرق صغير واقف على غصن الزيزفون.
examples.trans: There is a small blue bird perched on the linden branch.

examples.text: صوت الطيور بالساحة الصبح حلو كتير.
examples.trans: The sound of the birds in the courtyard in the morning is lovely.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عادية, plural: عاديين).

examples.trans: Bread with jam needs regular unsalted butter.
A quiet, ordinary day in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Can mean physically high or loud (for a voice or sound).

examples.trans: The music volume is very high.

examples.text: الرف العالي بالخزانة عليه كتب جدتي.
examples.trans: The high shelf in the cupboard holds my grandmother's books.

meanings.note: Geminate verb (بعد / عدّيت) from root ع-د-د. Takes -ey- before consonant-initial past suffixes.

examples.trans: I can count them quickly.
I counted the envelopes twice.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: I went to the doctor because I am sick.

examples.text: استعملنا ورق نشافة عشان الحبر ما يطبع.
examples.trans: We used blotting paper so the ink would not stain.

meanings.note: The standalone number ten.

examples.trans: The time is ten o'clock right now.
The shop closes at ten o'clock at night.

meanings.note: The number twenty.

examples.trans: He is twenty years old.

examples.text: المخبز بشتغل بنفس الوصفة من عشرين سنة.
examples.trans: The bakery has been using the same recipe for twenty years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عصافير.

examples.trans: We hear the birds in the tree.
We set out water for the birds in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: حطينا الخريطة على الطاولة وبلشنا نحللها.
examples.trans: We laid the map on the table and began analysing it.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفحص, بيفحص).

examples.trans: Tariq will inspect the cellar right away.
We checked the heater and pipes this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقول, بيقول).

examples.trans: What does clause fourteen say?
He said thank you and hung up!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'in front of, before'.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns against the evening sky.
The car is parked in front of the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Takes pronoun suffixes: كأنها ('as if it'), كأنهم ('as if they').

examples.text: بتحكي مع الجيران كأنهم صحاب زمان.
examples.trans: She talks with the neighbours as if they were old friends.
It sounded as if it came from the heating pipe.

meanings.note: Placed AFTER the adjective or verb it intensifies: تقيلة كتير ('very heavy'), شكرا كتير ('thank you very much').

examples.trans: The smell is so good!
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; كرت بريد means 'postcard'. Plural: كروت.

examples.text: بعتتله كرت بريد قصير الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I sent him a short postcard last week.
I recognised his neat handwriting on the card right away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كلمات.

examples.trans: She did not say a single word to anyone.
The word thank you warms the heart.

meanings.note: Refers to a literal treasure or something highly valued metaphorically.

examples.trans: They found an old treasure underground.

examples.text: الوصفات السرية اللي بالدفتر أغلى من أي كنز.
examples.trans: The secret recipes in the notebook are more precious than any treasure.

meanings.note: Takes pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian: لأني (because I), لأنك (because you), لأنه (because he/it — also general 'because'), لأنكم (because you pl.).

examples.text: لأنه القهوة الطيبة بتخلي الناس لطاف!
examples.trans: Because good coffee makes people pleasant!
Thank you because you kept the bag safe.

meanings.note: Invariant modal word followed by a subjunctive verb (without ب-) to express 'must / have to / need to'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everything has to be just right!

لاقى.gloss: to find; to encounter; to meet

meanings.en: to find; to encounter; to meet
meanings.note: Form III defective verb widely used in Jordanian Arabic as the everyday verb meaning to find (alongside لقي).

examples.text: أخيرا لاقينا المفتاح الضاع تحت السجادة.
examples.trans: We finally found the lost key under the rug.

examples.text: إذا دورت منيح بالدرج بتلاقي الكرت.
examples.trans: If you look carefully in the drawer you will find the card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلحق, بيلحق).

examples.trans: Follow me quickly to the third floor!

examples.text: لحقنا دكان الخردوات أول ما فتح.
examples.trans: We caught the hardware shop right as it opened.

meanings.note: An alternative spelling and pronunciation variant of 'لسا', used widely in the Levant.

examples.trans: I am still studying for the exam.

examples.text: مازن لسه عم بدور عالبطاقة الأخيرة بالدرج.
examples.trans: Mazen is still searching for the final card in the drawer.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: I haven't eaten anything since the morning.

examples.text: ما عرفت إنه العلبة فيها طابق سري من تحت.
examples.trans: I did not know that the box had a secret compartment underneath.

meanings.note: Form III active participle of حافظ; with على means preserving/maintaining, and standalone can mean conservative.

examples.text: المخبز محافظ على وصفته الأصلية من خمسين سنة.
examples.trans: The bakery has preserved its original recipe for fifty years.

examples.text: العسل البلدي محافظ على طعمه الطبيعي الصافي.
examples.trans: The local honey keeps its pure natural flavour.

meanings.note: Noun of place from خبز (to bake), with -ي ('my').

examples.text: ريحة الخبز الطازة طالعة من مخبز الحارة من الساعة ستة.
examples.trans: The smell of fresh bread has been wafting out of the neighborhood bakery since six.

examples.text: فتحت مخبزي الصغير بهالشارع قبل تلات سنين.
examples.trans: I opened my small bakery on this street three years ago.

meanings.note: Common defective verb for walking on foot or things running smoothly.

examples.text: ممنوع تمشي عكاحلك لحد بكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: You mustn't walk on your ankle until tomorrow morning.

examples.text: مشينا عالهدا بالساحة بعد ما وقفت المطر.
examples.trans: We walked gently across the courtyard after the rain stopped.

meanings.note: Noun of instance/manner from مشى; refers to a leisurely walk or someone's manner of walking.

examples.text: طلعنا بمشية خفيفة بالساحة بعد الغدا.
examples.trans: We went out for a light stroll in the courtyard after lunch.

examples.text: عرفته من مشيته السريعة قبل ما يلتفت.
examples.trans: I recognized him from his brisk gait before he turned around.

meanings.note: Form IV active participle of أضحك (to make laugh).

examples.text: طارق حكى موقف مضحك خلى الكل يضحك.
examples.trans: Tariq told a funny story that made everyone laugh.

examples.text: رسمة القط بالدفتر طلعت مضحكة كتير.
examples.trans: The drawing of the cat in the notebook turned out very funny.

meanings.note: Passive participle of نحت (to carve stone or wood); used for architectural reliefs and carved wooden items.

examples.text: في رقم منحوت على الحجر فوق البوابة.
examples.trans: There is a number carved into the stone above the gate.

examples.text: القوس المنحوت بالحيط قديم ومتقن كتير.
examples.trans: The carved arch in the wall is old and very finely crafted.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'good' and adverbially 'well' (نمت منيح؟ 'did you sleep well?').

examples.trans: It has a good, comfortable wooden bed.
Did you sleep well under the wooden ceiling?

meanings.note: Form II passive participle of هذّب (to refine manners); common praise for children and guests.

examples.text: طارق ولد مهذب وبحكي مع الكل باحترام.
examples.trans: Tariq is a polite boy and speaks to everyone respectfully.

examples.text: سلمت علينا بطريقة لطيفة ومهذبة كتير.
examples.trans: She greeted us in a very kind and polite manner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مواعيد.

examples.trans: I always appreciate punctuality.

examples.text: عندنا موعد مهم يوم الجمعة الظهر.
examples.trans: We have an important appointment Friday at noon.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word for water (feminine!). Before another noun in possession ('water of...'), becomes مية (mayyet): مية الدوش ('shower water'), مية الشتا ('winter water').

examples.trans: Please drink a glass of cold water.
The hot water is working again in the bathroom.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun used for people.

examples.trans: Who rang the bell?

examples.text: مين كتب هاي الملاحظة عالورقة بالحبر الأزرق؟
examples.trans: Who wrote this note on the paper in blue ink?

meanings.note: Used for decorative water fountains in parks or squares.

examples.trans: There is a beautiful fountain in the park.

examples.text: نافورة المي اللي بنص الساحة صوتها هادي ومريح.
examples.trans: The water fountain in the middle of the courtyard has a calm, soothing sound.

meanings.note: Used for the metal or objects made of it.

examples.trans: This jug is made of copper.

examples.text: الإبريق والمصفاية معمولين من نحاس مطروق قديم.
examples.trans: The teapot and strainer are made of old hammered copper.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian spelling/pronunciation of هذا ('this/that').

examples.text: هادا الكتاب من أحلى الروايات اللي قرأتها هالسنة.
examples.trans: This book is one of the best novels I've read this year.

examples.text: مين جاب هادا الفانوس الحلو عالطاولة؟
examples.trans: Who brought this lovely lantern onto the table?

meanings.note: Signature urban Jordanian/Levantine adverb for now (also spelled هلا in Jordan).

examples.text: هلق رح نفتح الصينية ونذوق أول قطعة.
examples.trans: Right now we will open the tin and taste the first piece.
We finished writing the notes just now.

meanings.note: Used in negative constructions or as a strong negative emphasis.

examples.trans: Not even one of them came.

examples.text: سألت الكل بس ولا حدا بيعرف وين حطوا المفتاح.
examples.trans: I asked everyone, yet not a single person knows where they put the key.

meanings.note: The standard interrogative adverb for location in the dialect.

examples.trans: Where are you going?

examples.text: وين حطيت مفاتيح السيارة بعد ما رجعت من الشغل؟
examples.trans: Where did you put the car keys after you got back from work?

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Oh Ahmed, come here.

examples.text: يا سيدي، تفضل اشرب معنا فنجان قهوة قبل ما تروح.
examples.trans: Sir, please come have a cup of coffee with us before you leave.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today is a long day.

examples.text: سافرنا عالعقبة وقعدنا هناك يوم كامل عالشط.
examples.trans: We traveled to Aqaba and spent a whole day there at the beach.
